searchDocs.content: </> InMemoryStore.failNext( self: InMemoryStore, operation: string, count: number? ) → () Makes the next count calls to operation fail, as a store outage would. Operation names are the method names: get, set, update, remove, sortedSet, sortedRemove, sortedRange.

searchDocs.title: conflictNext​
searchDocs.content: </> InMemoryStore.conflictNext( self: InMemoryStore, operation: string, count: number?, mutator: ((any) → any)?-- Receives the current value and returns the competing writer's value. Omit to re-run against unchanged state. ) → () Makes the next count updates lose a compare-and-set race. The transform runs once against the value it read, that result is discarded,mutator installs a competing write, and the transform runs again against the new value, which is what UpdateAsync does under contention. This is what catches a transform that fails to reset its own bookkeeping when re-entered, which every conditional write in Muster depends on.

searchDocs.title: spreadScore​
searchDocs.content: </> Matcher.spreadScore( candidates: {Candidate}, indexes: {number} ) → ( number, number ) The default scoring function: rating spread across individual members, then total queue time. Both are minimised, compared in that order. Spread is measured per member rather than per ticket, so a group with a wide internal skill gap is penalised accordingly. Returns a spread of 0 when no candidate carries a rating, leaving queue time as the whole ordering, which is the behaviour an unrated queue wants.

searchDocs.title: band​
searchDocs.content: </> Lanes.band( layout: Layout, lane: number ) → ( number, number ) The rating range lane covers, as a half-open [low, high). Infinite on the open ends, and infinite on both in hash mode.

searchDocs.title: laneFor​
searchDocs.content: </> Lanes.laneFor( layout: Layout, ticketId: string, rating: number? ) → number Which lane a ticket belongs to under layout. Deterministic, so two servers using the same layout agree without coordinating. rating is the ticket's party-aggregated rating and is only read in band mode, where it is what decides the lane. It is never absent there in practice, since a rated queue rejects a ticket without one; a missing rating falls into the lowest band.

searchDocs.title: legacyLanes​
searchDocs.content: </> Lanes.legacyLanes( layout: Layout, lane: number, previous: Layout? ) → {number} The lanes of previous that may hold tickets belonging to lane under layout. A worker reads their maps alongside its own while the old generation drains. Bands: a ticket's band follows from its rating, so the old lanes that can hold one of this lane's tickets are exactly those whose range overlaps this lane's. Layouts change by one boundary at a time, which makes that one old lane after a split and two after a merge. Hashes: both counts are powers of two, since the scaler only doubles or halves, which makes this exact. A ticket hashes to h % count: growing, a ticket in old lane o satisfies h % previous == o, so reading old lane lane % previous covers it; shrinking, h % count equals (h % previous) % count, so every old lane o with o % count == lane contributes. Either way the result holds at most previous.count / count entries.

searchDocs.title: Runtime
searchDocs.content: On this page Runtime This item is only intended to be used by the module's authors. Private Show Private The only module in Muster that touches a Roblox global. Everything else receives what it needs through configuration, which is what lets the whole engine run headlessly under Lune against fakes. Each global is read through an any-typed local so the same source typechecks under Roblox (where game exists) and runs under Lune (where it resolves to nil).

searchDocs.title: host​
searchDocs.content: </> QuickPlay.host( self: any, options: HostOptions ) → Result<HostedListing> Advertises this server as joinable. Call it once the match server is ready to take players, with whatever a joining server needs to reach you: queue.quickplay:host({ data = { accessCode = code, placeId = ARENA_PLACE } }) data is delivered verbatim as assignment.data and must survive a JSON round trip, within quickPlay.maxListingDataBytes (1024). capacity defaults to quickPlay.capacity, which defaults to size.max. The player count is read from playerCount on every heartbeat, defaulting to the Players service.

searchDocs.title: search​
searchDocs.content: </> QuickPlay.search( self: any, request: any-- partition, size, userIds. ) → Result<{ listingId: string, reservationId: string, listing: Listing }?> Looks for a seat and takes it. Returns ok(nil) when nothing joinable was found, which is the ordinary "everything is full" outcome and not an error: the caller stays queued.

searchDocs.title: release​
searchDocs.content: </> QuickPlay.release( self: any, listingId: string, reservationId: string ) → Result<boolean>-- False when the reservation was already gone. Hands a claimed seat back. Call it when the teleport you were holding it for did not happen.

searchDocs.title: listings​
searchDocs.content: </> QuickPlay.listings( self: any, partition: string? ) → Result<{ListingView}> The joinable listings in a partition, fullest first, for a server browser or a debug command. Reads every lane, so prefer QuickPlay:search for anything on a hot path.

searchDocs.title: get​
searchDocs.content: </> QuickPlay.get( self: any, listingId: string ) → Result<Listing?> Reads one listing record by id.

searchDocs.title: step​
searchDocs.content: </> QuickPlay.step( self: any, mono: number ) → () Heartbeats whichever hosted listings are due. Driven by the queue's worker pass, so queue:step() covers it.

searchDocs.title: hostedCount​
searchDocs.content: </> QuickPlay.hostedCount(self: any) → number Hosted listings on this server, for Matchmaker:health.

searchDocs.title: closeAll​
searchDocs.content: </> QuickPlay.closeAll(self: any) → () Delists everything this server is hosting. Called from Matchmaker:stop, so a match server bound to game:BindToClose stops taking players the moment it starts shutting down rather than after listingExpiration. A server that dies without this is cleaned up by expiry anyway; this only makes it immediate.

searchDocs.title: matched​
searchDocs.content: </> Matchmaker.matched: Signal<MatchEnvelope<T>> Fires on every server holding at least one of the matched players. Does not fire on a server holding none of them.

searchDocs.title: aborted​
searchDocs.content: </> Matchmaker.aborted: Signal<AbortContext> Fires when a match that had already claimed its tickets failed to commit. Its players return to the queue. See AbortReason.

searchDocs.title: queued​
searchDocs.content: </> Matchmaker.queued: Signal<Ticket> Fires on this server when a ticket is successfully enqueued here.

searchDocs.title: cancelled​
searchDocs.content: </> Matchmaker.cancelled: Signal<Ticket> Fires on this server when a ticket it was tracking is cancelled.

searchDocs.title: parties​
searchDocs.content: </> Matchmaker.parties: Party Cross-server parties sharing this queue's store. Built on first access and writes nothing until used; see Party.

searchDocs.title: quickPlayMatched​
searchDocs.content: </> Matchmaker.quickPlayMatched: Signal<QuickPlayAssignment<T>> Fires when a queued player is backfilled into a match that is already running, carrying the listing's published data. Only fires on the server that claimed the seat, which is the server holding the players. Requires the quickPlay config; on a queue without it, nothing ever fires here. See QuickPlay.

searchDocs.title: quickplay​
searchDocs.content: </> Matchmaker.quickplay: QuickPlay Backfilling into live matches, sharing this queue's store. Built on first access and writes nothing until used. Throws on a queue with no quickPlay config; see QuickPlay.

searchDocs.title: new​
searchDocs.content: </> Matchmaker.new(config: MatchmakerConfig) → any Builds a queue. name and size are required; see the configuration table on Matchmaker for the rest. Configuration problems throw rather than returning a Result, since they cannot be recovered from at runtime.

searchDocs.title: Errors
searchDocs.content: Type	Description"Muster: ..."	Reported at the call site, naming the offending field.

searchDocs.title: enqueue​
searchDocs.content: </> Matchmaker.enqueue( self: any, userId: number, options: EnqueueOptions? ) → Result<Ticket> Queues one player as a one-member ticket. On a rated queue, options.rating is required unless rating.default is configured; on an unrated queue, supplying one throws.

searchDocs.title: Errors
searchDocs.content: Type	Description"Muster: queue \"<name>\" is rated but no rating was given"	No rating and no default. "Muster: queue \"<name>\" is unrated, so `rating` cannot be supplied"	Rating passed to an unrated queue.

searchDocs.title: enqueueGroup​
searchDocs.content: </> Matchmaker.enqueueGroup( self: any, userIds: {number}, options: GroupOptions? ) → Result<Ticket> Queues a set of players as one ticket. The group is never split across matches and is matched at its aggregate rating. Takes userIds directly and does not involve Party. The first userId becomes the ticket's leader, and is the only one who may cancel or acknowledge it. queue:enqueueGroup({ leaderId, friendId }, { ratings = ratings }) Groups larger than size.max are rejected with InvalidPartySize, and a repeated userId with DuplicateMember.

searchDocs.title: enqueueParty​
searchDocs.content: </> Matchmaker.enqueueParty( self: any, partyId: string, requesterUserId: number, options: GroupOptions?-- ratings is keyed by userId. ) → Result<Ticket> Queues a Party by id. Only the party's leader may call this. The party's membership is locked for the lifetime of the ticket: invites, kicks, leaves, leadership transfers and disbanding all return PartyLocked until the ticket matches, is cancelled, or expires.

searchDocs.title: quickPlay​
searchDocs.content: </> Matchmaker.quickPlay( self: any, userId: number, options: EnqueueOptions? ) → Result<Ticket> Queues one player and looks for a live match to drop them into. This is Matchmaker:enqueue with quickPlay = true: an ordinary ticket is written, and a seat in an already-running match is searched for immediately and then every searchInterval afterwards. If every listed match is full the player simply waits in the normal queue, and forms a fresh match the usual way. The two outcomes race, so the return value is the ticket rather than the assignment; a backfill arrives on queue.quickPlayMatched, a fresh match on queue.matched. casual.quickPlayMatched:connect(function(assignment) TeleportService:TeleportToPrivateServer( assignment.data.placeId, assignment.data.accessCode, { player }) end) casual:quickPlay(player.UserId)

searchDocs.title: Errors
searchDocs.content: Type	Description"Muster: queue \"<name>\" has no Quick Play"	No `quickPlay` in the config.

searchDocs.title: quickPlayGroup​
searchDocs.content: </> Matchmaker.quickPlayGroup( self: any, userIds: {number}, options: GroupOptions? ) → Result<Ticket> Matchmaker:enqueueGroup with Quick Play, for a group that should backfill together. The group is never split: it takes as many seats in one listing as it has members, or it waits. A group larger than quickPlay.capacity can only ever form a fresh match.

searchDocs.title: cancel​
searchDocs.content: </> Matchmaker.cancel( self: any, requesterUserId: number, ticketId: string ) → Result<true> Cancels a ticket. Only the ticket's leader may cancel it, and only while its state isQueued. A ticket already claimed for a match returns NotQueued.

searchDocs.title: cancelForUser​
searchDocs.content: </> Matchmaker.cancelForUser( self: any, userId: number ) → Result<boolean>-- True if a ticket was cancelled, false if the user had none queued. Cancels whatever ticket a user currently holds, if any. Unlike Matchmaker:cancel, this looks the ticket up and cancels it as its leader, so it works for any member of a group. Connected to Players.PlayerRemoving unless autoCancelOnLeave is disabled.

searchDocs.title: getTicket​
searchDocs.content: </> Matchmaker.getTicket( self: any, userId: number ) → Result<Ticket?> The ticket a user currently holds, or nil. Tickets are exclusive across every queue sharing a namespace, so this returns a ticket even if the user queued somewhere else.

searchDocs.title: getStatus​
searchDocs.content: </> Matchmaker.getStatus( self: any, ticketId: string ) → Result<QueueStatus<T>> The state of a ticket: Queued, Claiming, Matched, Cancelled, or Expired. A Matched status carries the envelope.

searchDocs.title: getMatch​
searchDocs.content: </> Matchmaker.getMatch( self: any, matchId: string ) → Result<MatchEnvelope<T>?> Reads a committed match by id, or nil if there is no ready match under that id. Matches remain readable for matchExpiration (300 s), which covers a player who rejoined on another server and needs the envelope again.

searchDocs.title: acknowledge​
searchDocs.content: </> Matchmaker.acknowledge( self: any, requesterUserId: number, ticketId: string ) → Result<MatchEnvelope<T>> Releases a matched ticket's players so they may queue again, and unlocks its party. This happens automatically on delivery unless manualAcknowledge is set. Enable that setting to hold the reservation until you have confirmed whatever follows the match, such as a teleport. A failure then leaves the players free to re-queue rather than locked out until their reservation expires.

searchDocs.title: step​
searchDocs.content: </> Matchmaker.step(self: any) → () Runs one worker pass: ticket upkeep, lane acquisition, then a scan of each held lane. The worker thread calls this on a loop. Calling it directly advances the system one step, which is how the test suite drives it without yielding.

searchDocs.title: start​
searchDocs.content: </> Matchmaker.start(self: any) → () Starts the worker thread and subscribes for cross-server delivery. Called by the constructor unless autoStart is disabled. Calling it twice does nothing.

searchDocs.title: stop​
searchDocs.content: </> Matchmaker.stop(self: any) → () Stops the worker and releases every lane lease this server holds, so another server can take them immediately instead of waiting out the 15-second timeout. Suitable for game:BindToClose.

searchDocs.title: destroy​
searchDocs.content: </> Matchmaker.destroy(self: any) → () Calls Matchmaker:stop, disconnects the PlayerRemoving connection, and drops every signal handler.

searchDocs.title: health​
searchDocs.content: </> Matchmaker.health(self: any) → any A snapshot of this server's view of the queue, for logging or a debug command. Field Meaning localTickets Tickets this server enqueued and is still tracking. ownedLanes Lane leases this server currently holds. laneMode "auto" or "fixed". laneSplit "band" if lanes are rating ranges, "hash" if they are an even spread. laneCount Lanes the default partition is sharded into. laneBounds The rating boundaries between them, empty unless laneSplit is "band". laneChanges Resizes this server has applied. throttled True once 1% of requests have come back throttled. broadcastHealthy False while message delivery looks unreliable. broadcastsSent / broadcastsReceived Message counts since start. requests Per-structure successes, failures, throttles and mean latency. Values are local to this server, not fleet-wide.

searchDocs.title: Metadata​
searchDocs.content: </> type Metadata = {[string]: any} Caller-supplied data carried on a ticket. Must survive a JSON round trip through MemoryStore: strings, numbers, booleans, and tables of those. Functions, Instances, cycles, and tables mixing array and dictionary keys are rejected at enqueue withInvalidMetadata. Limited to maxMetadataBytes (1024).

searchDocs.title: Member​
searchDocs.content: </> interface Member { userId: number serverId: string-- JobId of the server that enqueued them; where their match is delivered. rating: number?-- Present if and only if the queue is rated. provisional: boolean?-- True when rating.default was substituted for a missing rating. metadata: Metadata? } One player within a ticket or a match. serverId is per-member rather than per-ticket because a party's members can be on different servers, and each is notified on their own.

searchDocs.title: Ticket​
searchDocs.content: </> interface Ticket { id: string queue: string partition: string partyId: string? leaderUserId: number members: {Member} size: number rating: number?-- Party-aggregated rating, absent on unrated queues. metadata: Metadata? queuedAt: number expiresAt: number state: "Queued" | "Claimed" | "Matched" | "Cancelled" | "QuickPlayed" matchId: string? lane: number-- Index within the partition. laneCount: number-- Lane count in force when the ticket was written; lanes scale at runtime. laneGeneration: number-- Which revision of the partition's lane layout that count belonged to. quickPlay: boolean?-- True when this ticket may also backfill into a live match. See QuickPlay. listingId: string?-- The listing a QuickPlayed ticket was backfilled into. } A queue entry covering one player or one group. A ticket is never split across matches.

searchDocs.title: MatchEnvelope​
searchDocs.content: </> interface MatchEnvelope { v: number-- Schema version. matchId: string queue: string partition: string createdAt: number size: number-- Total players across all members. members: {Member} ticketIds: {string} partyIds: {string} data: T-- The finalize hook's return value, or an empty table if there is no hook. } A committed match, delivered to every server holding one of its members. Generic over the finalizer's return type, so match.data.accessCode is typed and autocompletes. Deduplicate on matchId. The same set of players may appear under a second matchId if a worker stalled and its work was repaired.

searchDocs.title: MatchContext​
searchDocs.content: </> interface MatchContext { matchId: string queue: string partition: string members: {Member} ticketIds: {string} partyIds: {string} size: number averageRating: number?-- Mean member rating, absent on unrated queues. createdAt: number deadline: number-- Monotonic time the hook must return by. } The argument to a finalize hook: everything known about the match before the hook's own return value is attached.

searchDocs.title: AbortReason​
searchDocs.content: </> type AbortReason = "FinalizerError" | "FinalizerTimeout" | "FinalizerTooLarge" | "LeaseLost" | "StoreUnavailable" | "TicketStolen" Why a match that had already claimed its tickets failed to commit. Its players return to the queue in every case. Reason Cause FinalizerError The hook threw. FinalizerTimeout The hook did not return within finalizeTimeout. FinalizerTooLarge The hook's return value failed validation or exceeded maxMatchDataBytes. LeaseLost Another server took the lane while the hook was yielding. StoreUnavailable MemoryStore rejected the commit. TicketStolen A ticket was claimed by another match between selection and commit.

searchDocs.title: AbortContext​
searchDocs.content: </> interface AbortContext { matchId: string queue: string partition: string members: {Member} reason: AbortReason message: string?-- The hook's error text, when reason is FinalizerError. data: any?-- The hook's return value, if it produced one before the abort. } The argument to onAbort. When data is present, the hook ran to completion and its side effects outlived a match that never formed.

searchDocs.title: Finalizer​
searchDocs.content: </> type Finalizer = (context: MatchContext) → T Runs once per matchId, on the server that formed the match, after its tickets are claimed and before it commits. Expected to yield. The same set of players may be finalized again under a different matchId if this match aborts, so deduplicate on matchId.

searchDocs.title: AbortHandler​
searchDocs.content: </> type AbortHandler = (context: AbortContext) → ()

searchDocs.title: QueueStatus​
searchDocs.content: </> type QueueStatus = { state: "Queued", queuedAt: number } | {state: "Claiming"} | { state: "Matched", match: MatchEnvelope<T> } | { state: "QuickPlayed", listingId: string? } | {state: "Cancelled"} | {state: "Expired"}

searchDocs.title: ErrorCode​
searchDocs.content: </> type ErrorCode = string The codes a ServiceError can carry. Switch on this rather than on the message text, which is not stable.

searchDocs.title: ServiceError​
searchDocs.content: </> interface ServiceError { code: ErrorCode message: string retryable: boolean-- True when the same call may succeed on a later attempt. }

searchDocs.title: Result​
searchDocs.content: </> type Result = { ok: true, value: T } | { ok: false, error: ServiceError } Returned by every method that touches the network. Invalid configuration and invalid arguments throw instead. See Result.

searchDocs.title: SortedItem​
searchDocs.content: </> interface SortedItem { key: string value: any sortKey: number }

searchDocs.title: Store​
searchDocs.content: </> interface Store {} The storage contract, implemented by Muster.stores.MemoryStore against Roblox MemoryStore and by Muster.stores.InMemory against tables. Every method returns (success, value) and must not throw. update must be a compare-and-set: the transform may be invoked more than once for a single call, and returning nil from it must abort the write.

searchDocs.title: Subscription​
searchDocs.content: </> interface Subscription { disconnect: (self: any) → () }

searchDocs.title: Messaging​
searchDocs.content: </> interface Messaging {} The notification contract. Delivery is assumed to be best-effort and unordered; Muster never depends on a message arriving.

searchDocs.title: Candidate​
searchDocs.content: </> interface Candidate { ticketId: string partyId: string? size: number rating: number? ratings: {number} queuedAt: number } The reduced view of a ticket held in the lane index and passed to Matcher. Kept small because it is read far more often than the ticket record itself.

searchDocs.title: MatcherPolicy​
searchDocs.content: </> interface MatcherPolicy { minSize: number targetSize: number maxSize: number fallbackAfter: number-- Seconds before a below-target group is accepted. compatible: ( anchor: Candidate, candidate: Candidate, waitSeconds: number ) → boolean score: ( candidates: {Candidate}, indexes: {number} ) → ( number, number ) } Everything Matcher knows about how to group candidates. Supply one through the matcher config field to replace the rating window with role composition, region affinity, or any other rule. compatible decides whether a candidate may join an anchor's group. score returns (primary, secondary), both minimized and compared in that order. The built-in policy uses rating spread, then total queue time.

searchDocs.title: RatingConfig​
searchDocs.content: </> interface RatingConfig { window: number?-- Starting rating tolerance. Default 200. relax: number?-- Extra tolerance per second waited. Default 40. maxWindow: number?-- Ceiling on the widened window. Default infinite. unbounded: number?-- Seconds after which any rating matches. Default 60. default: number?-- Substituted when a caller omits a rating. Default nil, which makes omission an error. aggregate: (({number}) → number)?-- Party rating from member ratings. Default is a max-biased mean. } Supplying this table makes a queue rated. Omit it for an unrated queue, where tickets carry no rating and matching is oldest-first. Rated and unrated is a per-queue property: a rated queue requires a rating for every player, and an unrated one rejects them.

searchDocs.title: SizeConfig​
searchDocs.content: </> interface SizeConfig { min: number target: number? max: number? } Match sizing. size = 6 is shorthand for all three being 6, and target defaults to max. A group reaching target commits immediately. A smaller one waits fallbackAfter seconds, after which the largest group down to min is accepted.

searchDocs.title: EnqueueOptions​
searchDocs.content: </> interface EnqueueOptions { rating: number?-- Required on a rated queue unless rating.default is set. Throws on an unrated queue. metadata: Metadata? partition: string?-- Overrides partitionKey for this ticket. Partitions never match each other. serverId: string?-- Overrides where this member's match is delivered. Defaults to this server. quickPlay: boolean?-- Also let this ticket backfill into a live match. Requires the quickPlay config. }

searchDocs.title: GroupOptions​
searchDocs.content: </> interface GroupOptions { ratings: {[number]: number}?-- Per-userId ratings, required on a rated queue without a default. metadata: Metadata? partition: string?-- Overrides partitionKey for this ticket. serverIds: {[number]: string}?-- Per-userId delivery addresses, for members on other servers. quickPlay: boolean?-- Also let this ticket backfill into a live match. Requires the quickPlay config. }

searchDocs.title: PartyMember​
searchDocs.content: </> interface PartyMember { userId: number joinedAt: number serverId: string? }

searchDocs.title: PartyQueue​
searchDocs.content: </> interface PartyQueue { ticketId: string state: "Queued" | "Matched" matchId: string? expiresAt: number }

searchDocs.title: PartyView​
searchDocs.content: </> interface PartyView { id: string leaderUserId: number members: {PartyMember} createdAt: number version: number-- Incremented on every mutation; compare it to detect a stale read. queue: PartyQueue?-- Non-nil while queued, during which membership is frozen. }

searchDocs.title: PartyInvite​
searchDocs.content: </> interface PartyInvite { id: string partyId: string leaderUserId: number targetUserId: number createdAt: number expiresAt: number }

searchDocs.title: QuickPlayConfig​
searchDocs.content: </> interface QuickPlayConfig { capacity: number?-- Players a hosted match holds. Defaults to size.max. heartbeatInterval: number?-- Seconds between player-count refreshes. Default 30. listingExpiration: number?-- Seconds a listing survives without a heartbeat. Default 90. reservationTimeout: number?-- Seconds a claimed seat is held. Default 45. searchInterval: number?-- Seconds between search attempts by a queued ticket. Default 3. lanes: ("auto" | number)?-- Listing lane count. Default "auto". maxListingDataBytes: number?-- Budget for a listing's data. Default 1024. } Supplying this table, or true for all of its defaults, turns Quick Play on for a queue. Omit it and the feature is off: Matchmaker:quickPlay and queue.quickplay both throw. See QuickPlay.

searchDocs.title: Reservation​
searchDocs.content: </> interface Reservation { id: string size: number-- Seats held. userIds: {number}-- Who the seats are for. Used to retire the reservation once they arrive. expiresAt: number } A seat held in a listing between a claim and the player arriving. Counted against capacity for as long as it lives, so two lobbies cannot fill the same slot.

searchDocs.title: Listing​
searchDocs.content: </> interface Listing { v: number-- Schema version. id: string queue: string partition: string serverId: string-- JobId of the match server hosting it. capacity: number players: number-- Count at the last heartbeat, so up to heartbeatInterval stale. open: boolean-- False once the host has stopped taking players. reservations: {Reservation} data: T-- Whatever the host published: an access code, a place id, a map name. lane: number laneCount: number laneGeneration: number updatedAt: number expiresAt: number } One live match, advertised for backfill. Generic over the host's data, so listing.data.accessCode is typed.

searchDocs.title: ListingView​
searchDocs.content: </> interface ListingView { listingId: string serverId: string capacity: number free: number-- Seats free as of the last write. A hint, not a guarantee. updatedAt: number } The reduced copy of a listing held in the lane index, kept small because it is read far more often than the listing itself. free is what the index is sorted by, ascending, so the fullest joinable match is returned first.

searchDocs.title: HostOptions​
searchDocs.content: </> interface HostOptions { data: T-- Published to whoever joins. Put the access code and place id here. capacity: number?-- Overrides quickPlay.capacity for this match. partition: string?-- Only searchers on the same partition find it. Defaults to "all". players: number?-- Starting player count. Defaults to playerCount(). playerCount: (() → number)?-- Read on every heartbeat. Defaults to the Players service. presentUserIds: (() → {number})?-- Who is in the match now, used to retire fulfilled reservations. listingId: string?-- Reuse a known id, so a restarted host adopts its own listing. } The argument to QuickPlay:host.

searchDocs.title: QuickPlayAssignment​
searchDocs.content: </> interface QuickPlayAssignment { listingId: string reservationId: string-- Pass to QuickPlay:release if the teleport fails. queue: string partition: string serverId: string-- The match server hosting the listing. members: {Member} ticketId: string-- The ticket this assignment consumed. size: number data: T-- The listing's published data. } Delivered on queue.quickPlayMatched when a queued player is backfilled into a live match. Unlike a MatchEnvelope this fires only on the server that claimed the seat, since that is the server holding the players.

searchDocs.title: Logger​
searchDocs.content: </> type Logger = ( level: "info" | "warn" | "error", message: string, fields: {[string]: any} ) → ()

searchDocs.title: Metrics​
searchDocs.content: </> type Metrics = ( name: string, value: number, tags: {[string]: any} ) → ()
